key_insight: A multi-scale ML framework can jointly model chemical, spin, and structural disorder in alloys, enabling accurate prediction of phase transitions in highly complex magnetic materials.
engineering_relevance: This approach provides a practical simulation tool for designing and screening disordered alloys for thermal stability, magnetism, and structure-sensitive applications.
method: Combine graph neural networks and machine-learning interatomic potentials
Couple Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics for multi-scale statistical sampling
Model Fe-Co and Fe-Co-C as a testbed for coupled chemical, spin, and lattice disorder
evidence_signal: The framework predicts the Fe-Co order-disorder transition at 1,000 K and melting at 1,690 K, closely matching experimental values of 1,006 K and about 1,700 K.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the quality and transferability of the training data/models, especially when extending to alloys with more complex disorder landscapes.
paper_title: A Multi-Scale Machine Learning Framework for Coupled Chemical, Spin, and Structural Disorder in Alloys
